sb_prompt: PLEASE DISCUSS CREDIT CARDS.  FIND OUT HOW THE OTHER CALLER MAKES USE OF CREDIT CARDS.  HOW DO THEY COMPARE TO YOUR OWN?
turns: So, how are you with credit cards? Do you even use them much?
I use them a lot, actually, mostly for groceries and maybe one or two clothes things.
Well, that's interesting, I mostly just pay in cash, honestly.
That's really strange for your age, don't you think? My mom actually has a huge one, and she can barely keep up with the interest, which is kind of scary.
Yeah, I guess I'm lucky my credit score stayed low so I don't have to worry about that.
Oh wow, that's a scary way to think about it, but honestly my mom is really stressing out about it right now.
Yeah, you know, I figure if you don't pay it off every month, it just feels like money you're never actually getting back.
Yeah, exactly, it feels like you're just borrowing from the future and not really getting anything for it.
Right, and do you actually pay that off every month, or does it just sit there?
I do pay them off every month, usually by the 10th, otherwise it just spirals out of control.
That's good, really glad you're keeping on top of it.
Yeah, that's why I keep a separate checking account just for the cards, so I can't accidentally carry a balance.
That's smart, honestly, I think a lot of people just let the minimum payment slide and end up paying way more than they should.
Yeah, but I still don't get why anyone would use them for anything else if they can just pay cash.
Well, it's just easier sometimes to buy something and know I can pay for it later without carrying a heavy wallet around.
Yeah, but there's something that really bothers me about all the interest fees if you let them pile up.
I guess it's just that sometimes I need a little breathing room to make ends meet, even if I pay it off next month.
Yeah, but I still don't see how paying it off immediately makes the debt itself any less real than if I just bought the stuff with cash.
Yeah, but it's just that having it available makes me feel safer even if I'm not using the debt.
That's true, I guess it does give you a safety net, but it still feels like you're playing a dangerous game.
Yeah, I know it sounds risky, but sometimes the safety net is the only thing keeping me from falling.
Yeah, but I still can't shake the feeling that carrying that safety net is just inviting trouble, you know?
Yeah, I guess I just hope the safety net stays intact for a while longer.
Yeah, I just worry that having it sitting there, even if I'm not using it, feels like I'm walking a tightrope waiting for something to tip the scale.
I guess it's just that I don't trust myself to walk that tightrope without a net, to be honest.
Yeah, but if you don't trust yourself with a net, why not just learn to walk the rope instead?
I guess I'll keep the net tied on until I can figure out how to walk without one.
Yeah, but maybe you never will, either way.
I guess I'll just be careful, even if I do have the net.
Look, I just don't see the point in walking the tightrope if you're never going to figure out how to walk on the ground anyway.
You know, maybe I'm just too scared to leave it tied on.
I guess you're just too scared to leave it tied on.
I guess I'll just stick to cash then.
Yeah, looks like I'm sticking with cash after all.
Okay, well I'm definitely sticking to cash.
